title: Counting and grouping
objective: Group items in one pass by giving each a key that matching items share.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): hash tables

simplifies: Sorting each word costs a little (k log k for a word of k letters). Counting the letters instead is another common key; the grouping idea is the same.

quiz.prompt: Which key puts "listen" and "silent" in the same group?

options.explanation: Right. Both sort to the same letters, so they share a key.
"listen" starts with l and "silent" with s.
Length alone would also group "listen" with "orange".

quiz.prompt: Why use a dict instead of comparing every pair of words?

options.text: One pass with a dict lookup per word, instead of checking every pair
options.explanation: Right. That is about n steps rather than about n² pairs.
Dicts keep insertion order, not sorted order; the speed comes from the lookups.
